newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on export inspections, cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on export inspections, cash.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on bullish input from USDA's weekly export inspections data plus signals that commercials remain tight holders of cash wheat stocks, traders said.
"The wheat export number was higher than expected and that popped wheat," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

USDA Monday said 33.588 million bushels of wheat were inspected for export during the week ended September 5. That was well above the 26.586 million the previous week and above trader expectations for 22.0 million to 26.0 million bushels.
Actions by commercials lent support to prices.
"A lot of them in wheat were short and there are no deliveries," a trader said.

Deliveries of wheat on the September contract remain nearly non-existent with just 10,000 bushels posted Monday. Ideas circulated before the delivery cycle started that up to five million bushels of wheat eventually may be posted for delivery.
News Egypt bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat also was supportive.
Wheat closed seven cents a bushel higher to one cent lower, with September up seven at $4.53-1/2 a bushel.
Commercial buying in the December led to ideas that other export business soon may be announced, they said.

Term Commodities bought 1.5 million bushels of December, Refco Inc bought 1.0 million December while Tenco Inc bought 1.5 million December, traders said. In late trading, R.J. O'Brien bought one million bushels of December, they said.
Signs the wheat market was oversold and unwinding of bean/wheat and corn/wheat spreads lent additional support, they said.
"It had been hit pretty hard recently and today they just started to turn it around," a trader said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 15,000, up from 12,759 Friday.
In the wheat options pit, Cargill Investor Services sold 200 December $4.50 calls at 12-1/2 cents and Produce Grain sold 200 December $4.70 calls at eight cents, floor sources said.
Options volume was estimated at 3,500, up from 3,163 Friday.
